Commodore 64.fact: The C64 uses a complicated memory-banking scheme; the normal power-on default is the BASIC ROM mapped in at $A000–$BFFF, and the screen editor (KERNAL) ROM at $E000–$FFFF. If the KERNAL ROM is swapped out, BASIC will be removed at the same time.

Commodore 64.subject: Telecom & Postal
Commodore 64.question: BASIC is not active without the _____; BASIC often calls KERNAL routines, and part of the ROM code for BASIC is in the KERNAL ROM
Commodore 64.fact: If the KERNAL ROM is swapped out, BASIC will be removed at the same time. BASIC is not active without the KERNAL; BASIC often calls KERNAL routines, and part of the ROM code for BASIC is in the KERNAL ROM.

Commodore 64.question: The character ROM may be mapped into $D000–$_____, where it is then visible to the CPU
Commodore 64.fact: The character ROM may be mapped into $D000–$DFFF, where it is then visible to the CPU. By removing I/O from the memory map, $D000–$DFFF becomes free RAM.

Commodore 64.fact: The character ROM may be mapped into $D000–$DFFF, where it is then visible to the CPU. By removing I/O from the memory map, $D000–$DFFF becomes free RAM.
